These do not establish Putin's personal order for each event.","closed_system_silence":"High risk because independent media and civil society were restricted, increasing the chance that domestic safeguards or misconduct were unreported.","duplicate_reporting":"E002/E003 are separate HRW publications, not independent families. Internal safeguards and mitigating governance evidence remain incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Independent Russian-language technical nuclear-safety reporting, internal safeguards records, expert-governance evidence, and chain-of-command documentation are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E001 establishes formal authority; E022/E023 provide external checks on selected signaling and treaty procedures. Implementation of safeguards and internal controls remains independently unverified.","open_system_complaint_volume":"International monitoring may overrepresent visible external incidents, but this is secondary to concealed-risk concerns and does not negate documented facility exposure.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Facility exposure, formal authority, external conflict shocks, and arms-control baseline are addressed. Internal governance, population exposure beyond facilities, and target-period attribution remain incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E001","E006","E007","E008","E009","E010","E021","E022","E023","E034"],"unresolved_risks":["Personal attribution remains partly inferential.","Internal safeguards and expert deliberations are not documented.","Closed-system silence limits negative inference."]},"chapter_id":"1B","defensible_evidence_estimate":9,"independent_source_family_estimate":7,"missing_themes":["Internal safeguards and expert governance","Chain-of-command or personal attribution evidence","Independent technical assessment of dual-use and facility-risk management"],"substantive_issues":["Material attribution and governance gaps remain research-recoverable.","Facility-risk evidence should not be presented as proof of a personal order by Putin."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E005 is an ICJ order; E011 contains commission findings; E012 concerns an ICC warrant based on reasonable grounds; E034 is an indictment. E040/E041 document diplomacy and cooperation without proving good faith or durable restraint.","closed_system_silence":"High risk because restricted reporting and conflict-access limitations may conceal military misconduct, internal dissent, or failed remedies.","duplicate_reporting":"E005, E011, E012, E016, E039, E040, and E041 are distinct institutional publications, but overlapping underlying events require claim-level deduplication. E002/E003 are not independent families.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both adverse and contrary material is present: E040 and E041 document negotiated cooperation and diplomatic alternatives, while E005, E011, E012, and E047 document adverse conduct or attribution. Internal alternatives and tested official counterclaims remain missing.","missing_source_type":"Internal decision records, proxy-control evidence, local-language conflict reporting, and independent evidence of remedy implementation are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E001 and E047 support formal authority and a decision chain; E005, E011, E012, and E039 provide external checks. Proxy control, internal deliberation, and implementation of remedies remain unverified.","open_system_complaint_volume":"International conflict monitoring can concentrate reports where access and scrutiny are greatest; complaint volume is not a prevalence estimate, though documented findings remain material.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Conflict exposure, legal orders, formal authority, diplomatic alternatives, and external shocks are addressed. Proxy control, inherited military baseline, remedy, and counterfactual alternatives remain incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E001","E005","E011","E012","E016","E039","E040","E041","E047"],"unresolved_risks":["Attribution for subordinate or proxy conduct remains incomplete.","Remedy evidence shows gaps but not responsibility for denial.","Internal deliberations and official counterclaims are insufficiently tested."]},"chapter_id":"2B","defensible_evidence_estimate":10,"independent_source_family_estimate":8,"missing_themes":["Internal deliberations and decision alternatives","Proxy or subordinate control","Implementation of remedy and corrective action","Independent testing of official counterclaims"],"substantive_issues":["Major events are documented, but attribution and remedy remain incomplete.","Negotiated cooperation should remain bounded contrary evidence, not general exculpation."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E024-E027 document reported arrests, violence, laws, and accountability pressure; they are not uniformly adjudicated findings. Local government-actor violence remains insufficient for personal attribution without a direction, tolerance, or authority nexus.","closed_system_silence":"High risk because criminalized dissent, surveillance, self-censorship, and civil-society exit suppress reporting of abuse and national prevalence.","duplicate_reporting":"E002/E003 are one HRW family. E024 and E025 independently document protest repression but may overlap in protest events; E026 and E027 address different themes.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse evidence is broad and now includes vulnerable groups and remedy pressure. A targeted search for lawful restraint, effective remedies, and official claims independently tested remains incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Independent domestic or local-language monitoring from inside Russia, prison-condition and remedy records, and denominator-based national prevalence data are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E001 supports formal authority, but no independent verification of official justifications, restraint claims, or remedy performance is documented.","open_system_complaint_volume":"High risk for apparent severity and prevalence because accessible international and civil-society reporting may overrepresent observable complaints. OVD-Info explicitly cautions that reporting volume reflects observer access.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Protesters, journalists, monitors, and LGBT+ people are represented, and the invasion/mobilization shocks are identified. E019 is inherited baseline evidence, not a 2022 finding.","closed_system_silence":"High risk because media closures, surveillance, criminalized dissent, and self-censorship can conceal electoral and accountability failures.","duplicate_reporting":"E002/E003 are one HRW family. E028/E029 are separate Golos publications with overlapping observation networks and should not be treated as fully independent event sets. E019 is a distinct inherited baseline.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse 2022 contestability evidence and inherited technically competent administration are both present. A complete search for favorable institutional checks, appointments, succession, and effective remedies is not documented.","missing_source_type":"2022 appointment and succession records, independent institutional-accountability outcomes, local-language investigative reporting, and official claims with independent verification are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E001 establishes formal authority but not accountability. E028/E029 provide independent domestic monitoring; institutional checks and official claims remain incompletely tested.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Golos explicitly warns that report volume reflects observer activity and cannot measure total misconduct. External scrutiny may still concentrate visible complaints in a restricted information environment.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"E019 supplies inherited baseline; E028/E029 supply target-period election evidence; E002/E003 supply restrictions. The separation between inherited constraints, 2022 change, appointments, and succession remains incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E001","E002","E003","E019","E024","E025","E027","E028","E029","E046"],"unresolved_risks":["Appointments and succession remain uncovered.","Inherited baseline versus 2022 deterioration is only partly separated.","Closed-system silence limits negative inference.","Institutional remedy outcomes are missing."]},"chapter_id":"4B","defensible_evidence_estimate":10,"independent_source_family_estimate":6,"missing_themes":["2022 appointments and succession","Institutional accountability and remedy outcomes","Complete official and contrary evidence audit"],"substantive_issues":["Target-period election evidence materially improves the chapter but does not resolve succession or institutional-accountability gaps.","E019 must remain inherited context only."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E013/E017 are official instructions, not implementation findings. E014/E015/E035 overlap in macroeconomic shock and contraction analysis. E032 and E033 are one Treasury family; E034 is distinct.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both policy-response and adverse-shock evidence are present through E013, E014/E015/E035, and E036. Distributional harms, implementation failures, capture, enrichment, and correction were not systematically searched.","missing_source_type":"Household and regional distribution data, independent implementation audits, procurement and ownership findings, and local-language reporting are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E013/E017 are official intent evidence. E014/E015/E035 independently assess macro conditions; E036/E048 provide institutional response evidence but do not independently verify presidential authorship or household delivery.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Not the principal risk because the main evidence is macroeconomic rather than complaint-count based. Visible household complaints could nevertheless overrepresent accessible or politically salient hardship.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Formal direction, sanctions, war shock, macro outcomes, and Central Bank response are addressed. Household distribution, regional exposure, inherited baseline, implementation, and correction remain unclear.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E013","E014","E015","E032","E034","E035","E036","E048"],"unresolved_risks":["Aggregate outcomes cannot stand in for household welfare or ruler effectiveness.","War and sanctions confound attribution.","Capture, enrichment, delivery, and correction evidence remain incomplete."]},"chapter_id":"5B","defensible_evidence_estimate":8,"independent_source_family_estimate":6,"missing_themes":["Household and regional distribution","Independent implementation and delivery audit","Directly attributed capture or enrichment findings","Correction and adaptive response"],"substantive_issues":["The chapter has improved source breadth but still lacks delivery and distribution evidence.","E045 remains discovery-only and cannot support the estimate."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E013/E017 establish stated support instructions, not delivery. E037/E038/E043 provide country or institutional outcomes and actions, not personal responsibility. No adjudicated adverse or favorable ruler-specific finding is presented.","closed_system_silence":"High risk because restricted monitoring can conceal unequal access, service failures, politicization, and mortality-reporting problems.","duplicate_reporting":"E013/E017 are one Kremlin source family. E037/E042/E043 are WHO-family materials; E042 is a weak lead and should not be counted as a strong standalone unit. E014/E015 are economic context, not independent health-delivery evidence.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Favorable intent and limited institutional action are present through E013 and E043. A balanced search for delivery failure, equity, affordability, durable outcomes, and corrective response remains incomplete.","missing_source_type":"Independent health-system delivery audits, regional and household equity data, mortality and immunization validation, affordability evidence, and local-language or NGO monitoring are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E013 is official intent; E037/E038 and WHO materials provide independent outcome and data-quality context. They do not independently verify delivery, reach, or presidential contribution.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Secondary risk. International reporting may overrepresent accessible or salient failures, but the stronger risk is underreporting and unreliable denominators in a restricted system.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Beneficiaries, macro shocks, health-system data limitations, and one target-period pilot are addressed. Actual reach, subgroup equity, regional exposure, inherited baseline, durability, and correction remain unresolved.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E013","E014","E015","E036","E037","E038","E043"],"unresolved_risks":["Direct independent evidence of delivery and equity remains absent.","Country-level outcomes cannot establish ruler-attributed performance.","Closed-system silence and mortality-data limitations materially reduce confidence."]},"chapter_id":"6B","defensible_evidence_estimate":6,"independent_source_family_estimate":4,"missing_themes":["Delivery quality and population reach","Equity and affordability","Independent mortality and immunization validation","Politicization, correction, and durability"],"substantive_issues":["The continuation improved domain coverage but not ruler attribution or delivery verification.","Missing evidence is not evidence of poor performance."]},{"attribution_risk":"high","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E030/E031 are investigative and network-level allegations; E032/E033 are Treasury sanctions designations, not criminal judgments; E046 establishes a transparency restriction, not enrichment; E047 concerns a policy decision rather than integrity. No final adjudication is present.","closed_system_silence":"Very high risk because media restrictions, NGO exit, surveillance, and self-censorship can suppress corruption detection and publication.","duplicate_reporting":"E030, E031, and E044 overlap in LLCInvest/Putin-linked network research and must not count as three independent families. E032/E033 are one Treasury family. E018 is a context lead, not additional proof.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Adverse personal/network evidence is now substantial but not adjudicated. Favorable evidence is limited to official declarations or denials, with no systematic search for exculpatory financial records, independent audits, or lawful asset explanations.","missing_source_type":"Court or enforcement findings, independently verified asset and beneficial-ownership records, procurement evidence, appointment/conflict-of-interest records, and local-language investigative corroboration are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E032/E033 are official sanctions findings with stated evidentiary bases but no independent judicial check. E046 is an official transparency notice. No credible independent exculpatory check is documented.","open_system_complaint_volume":"Open investigations may overrepresent opposition-linked or visible allegations and make severity appear higher. This does not convert allegations into findings and is secondary to severe closed-system underreporting.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Network exposure, alleged personal nexus, official opacity, and target-period context are addressed. Personal ownership/benefit, appointment pathways, inherited wealth, and 2022-specific conduct remain incompletely established.","supporting_evidence_ids":["E018","E030","E031","E032","E033","E044","E046"],"unresolved_risks":["The personal nexus is credible but remains partly contested and non-adjudicated.","Opacity is not proof of concealment motive.","A bounded search for court findings, financial records, and independent corroboration could materially improve the dossier."]},"chapter_id":"7B","defensible_evidence_estimate":4,"independent_source_family_estimate":3,"missing_themes":["Adjudicated personal-integrity findings","Verified ownership and beneficial-ownership records","Appointment or conflict-of-interest nexus","Independent favorable or exculpatory evidence"],"substantive_issues":["The chapter is no longer empty, but the evidence remains allegation- and designation-heavy.","Continuation is warranted because attribution and adjudication gaps are research-recoverable."]},{"attribution_risk":"medium","bias_review":{"allegations_vs_findings":"E013/E017 are official instructions; E034 is an indictment; E036/E048 are institutional reports; E016 is analysis; E035 is macro context. These establish intent, assigned responsibility, or institutional action, not successful implementation or durable progress.","closed_system_silence":"High risk because restricted reporting can conceal bureaucratic distortion, implementation failure, dissenting performance information, and lack of correction.","duplicate_reporting":"E013/E017 are one source family. E035 and E036 are distinct institutions but overlap in crisis-response context. E037/E042/E043 are WHO-family materials. E034, E040, E041, E043, and E048 address distinct operational themes but some outcomes remain institutionally rather than ruler attributed.","favorable_and_adverse_search":"Both favorable and adverse material is present: E036, E040, E043, and E048 document institutional action or cooperation, while E025, E034, and E035 document coercive execution, procurement failure, and adverse outcomes. Independent audits, competence comparisons, correction, and durable results remain incompletely searched.","missing_source_type":"Independent implementation audits, bureaucratic competence measures, subnational delivery data, procurement oversight, and local-language performance reporting are missing.","official_claim_independence":"E013/E017 are official intent; E036/E048 provide institution-specific implementation evidence; E034 and E035 provide external checks in narrower areas. No comprehensive independent audit of the governing portfolio is present.","open_system_complaint_volume":"International analysis may overrepresent visible or politically salient failures. More consequentially, restricted scrutiny may hide performance failures and suppress complaint reporting.","population_exposure_authority_baseline_shocks":"Formal authority, assigned bodies, war and sanctions shocks, selected implementation actions, and limited cooperation are addressed. gateway-only and discovery-only items remain excluded.","Closed-system silence is the principal cross-chapter bias, and absence of domestic reporting is not exculpatory.","Local facts are appropriately treated as contextual priors with attribution warnings; unused local facts are not evidence defects.","Several promising candidates remain unfetched or lack precise locators, including E042 and E045; these are recoverable research tasks where relevant.","Continuation should remain bounded to the selected lenses and focus on attribution, contrary evidence, precise locators, remedy, delivery, adjudication, and target-period separation."],"needs_continuation":true,"reviewer_summary":"All eight selected chapters require bounded continuation. The continuation round materially improved event coverage and source breadth, but did not resolve the principal risks: closed-system silence, incomplete ruler attribution, limited contrary and favorable searches, and weak independent verification of implementation or remedy. Chapter 7B now has credible but non-adjudicated personal/network evidence; Chapter 6B remains weak on delivery and attribution. Missing evidence is not treated as negative ruler evidence.","schema_version":"ruler_evidence_review_v1","selected_theme_ids":["1B","2B","3B","4B","5B","6B","7B","8B"]}
